title: Incorrect Warehouse Inventory Allocation
business_scenario: Multiple regional warehouses store varying stock of a requested product, with existing reservations.
symptoms: Greedy allocation assigns stock from warehouses whose stock is already reserved, over-allocates inventory, or violates warehouse fulfillment priorities.
reproduction_steps: Create warehouse inventory records with existing reservedStock.
Request an allocation for quantity Q.
Inspect the resulting warehouse allocations and reservedStock counts.
expected_behavior: Allocation algorithm must calculate net available stock (stock - reservedStock) for each warehouse, sort by fulfillment priority, and allocate without exceeding net availability.
actual_behavior: The greedy algorithm checks raw stock ignoring reservedStock and sorts arbitrarily, resulting in over-allocation of reserved units.
root_cause: warehouse.service.js uses inv.stock instead of Math.max(0, inv.stock - inv.reservedStock) and fails to order warehouses by priority.
acceptance_criteria: Warehouse allocation must never exceed net available stock and must respect warehouse priority rankings.
reference_fix: Sort inventories by warehouse priority ascending, compute net available = stock - reservedStock, and track reservations in warehouse.service.js.
regression_tests: Single warehouse allocation fulfills successfully when stock is sufficient.
